import_prompt_intro: I need a study plan split by day. The answer must be only valid JSON, with no text before or after, in this format:
import_prompt_rules: Rules: "date" is the day the task gets done and "due" is a deadline; both are optional and use YYYY-MM-DD. "subject" must be exactly one of these subjects: {subjects} (or be left out). "priority" can be none, low, medium, or high. "subtasks" is an optional list of strings. Keep titles short and concrete. Today is {today}. Spread the workload evenly across the days.
import_prompt_rules_no_subjects: Rules: "date" is the day the task gets done and "due" is a deadline; both are optional and use YYYY-MM-DD. "subject" is not needed. "priority" can be none, low, medium, or high. "subtasks" is an optional list of strings. Keep titles short and concrete. Today is {today}. Spread the workload evenly across the days.

privacy_description: What data Tilde stores, where, why, and how to delete it.
privacy_lead: Tilde only stores what it needs to work: your account and what you add to the app. It isn't sold, shared or used for ads.
privacy_data_1: From your Google account: your name, email address and profile picture, to show which account you're signed in with. Tilde never gets your password and can't read your email, Drive or Google Calendar.
privacy_data_2: What you add to the app: courses, schedule, to-dos, dates, grades, study sessions and settings.
privacy_data_3: For notes, only the link and name are stored: the files stay where they were. For a linked calendar, its address is stored so it can be downloaded again when you import its dates.
privacy_where_1: On Supabase (database and sign-in), on servers in the United States. The app is served by Vercel. Connections are always encrypted.
privacy_where_2: Every piece of data is tied to its account: the database only lets that same account read or change it.
privacy_use_1: Only to make the app work. It isn't sold, shared with third parties or used for ads. The database is only looked at by hand to fix a technical problem.
privacy_device_1: So the app opens offline, your browser keeps a copy of your data and screens, plus changes made offline until they're uploaded. It also remembers your language, theme and color. Signing out removes what was saved for your account.
privacy_device_2: The only cookies are the session ones and the language one. There are no third-party, advertising or analytics cookies.
privacy_delete_1: Settings → Delete account instantly deletes your account and everything in it. Database backups may keep it for a few more days, until they're replaced.
privacy_delete_2: You can also remove Tilde's access from your Google account settings.
privacy_changes_1: If this policy changes, this page and its date are updated.
terms_lead: Tilde is a free tool for organizing university life, built as a personal project. Using it means accepting these terms.
terms_account_1: You sign in with a Google account. What you add is yours, and you can delete it at any time from Settings.
terms_use_1: Tilde is for personal use. Trying to access other accounts' data, overloading the service or using it for anything illegal isn't allowed. Accounts that do may be suspended.
terms_warranty_1: It's provided as is, without warranties: it may have bugs, change or stop being available. Double-check important dates (finals, due dates, holidays) with your university: holidays are calculated and may not match the official ones.
terms_warranty_2: The people behind Tilde aren't liable for data loss or for anything resulting from using it.
terms_privacy_1: What's stored and how it's handled is in the <link>privacy policy</link>.
terms_changes_1: These terms may change; the date above shows the latest version. Using Tilde after a change means accepting it.
